heard: Our solar system is drifting through a massive hollow cavity. Roughly 15 ancient supernovas blasted this hole 1,000 light years wide. It's filled with thin plasma heated to a million degrees. Deep-sea crust on Earth still holds radioactive iron from those explosions. This giant bubble triggered the birth of every nearby star. New-born star nurseries like Taurus sit on its shell, expanding outward. Surprisingly, our sun didn't create this space. We just entered it recently, leaving us drifting right through its million-degree center.
